**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.

**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
`.env` (your own key), then:

```bash
uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
```

**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a
memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them.

## Hello World (local, 3 commands)

No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs.
The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After
`uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above):

```bash
# terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`)
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package
# terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key> uv run arena play case:S01 -v
```

It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it
in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation.

## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)

Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
```

Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
those headers, the body as raw JSON.

```bash
# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'

# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'

# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
the clock running.

## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap

The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
is for you, not for the agent).

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

## Choosing a model

`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
back to the naive move instead of losing the case.

## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
```

`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).

`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.

Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

## MCP server over the data

A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,
`get_case`.

```bash
uv run arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package   # speaks MCP on stdin/stdout
```

Add it to a client, e.g. Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add arena-data -- uv run --directory /path/to/starter-kit arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package
```

or any client with an `mcpServers` config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"arena-data": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/starter-kit",
  "arena", "mcp", "--data", "/path/to/data/package"]}}}
```

## Good to know

- **60 s per message**, per thread. A late message counts as a timeout (your last offer repeated);
  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.
- **Invalid messages cost nothing**: `422` and no round used. `409` means the thread or case has
  ended, or you were late.
- **Your key is your team's.** Keep `.env` out of git.
- Tests: `uv run pytest`. Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

### Lists and boards

- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.

- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

"""The naive buyer: anchors a little low, splits the difference, accepts early.

A baseline to beat, not a strategy: it ignores the data and the documents, never trades, never
asks and never walks away. One term sheet per e-mail.
"""

from ..cost import complete_offer, total_cost
from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing


class NaiveAgent:
    def __init__(self, anchor=0.10, close_gap=0.01):
        self.anchor, self.close_gap = anchor, close_gap

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        # Talk to the supplier whose standing term sheet costs least.
        quoting = [s for s in live_threads(threads) if standing(threads[s])[1].get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not quoting:
            return {
                "supplier_id": live_threads(threads)[0],
                "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}},
            }
        sid = min(quoting, key=lambda s: total_cost(case, standing(threads[s])[1]))
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
        accept = {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
        }
        theirs = terms["unit_price"]
        mine = [
            m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"]
            for m in events
            if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")
        ]
        if latest(events).get("status") in {"agreed", "final_offer"} or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
            return accept
        if not mine:
            price = theirs * (1 - self.anchor)
        elif theirs - mine[-1] <= theirs * self.close_gap:
            return accept
        else:
            price = (theirs + mine[-1]) / 2
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})}],
            },
        }
"""An LLM buyer that negotiates by e-mail: the model reads, argues and writes; code does numbers.

Code prepares the case, the letter that started it, the data rows the case points to, the cost C
of every standing term sheet (with the standard terms read from the supplier's quote PDF) and the
text of every attached document. The model writes the e-mail - arguments with data IDs included -
and proposes up to three term sheets. Code completes and snaps the term sheets, removes data IDs
that do not exist (an unknown ID costs trust), and refuses an accept that breaks a must-have or
loses to the alternative. Finding the data that moves a supplier is left to you: this agent only
sees what the case points to. Any provider works: pass `complete(system, user) -> str`, or use
`llm_from_env()`.
"""

import json
import logging
import math
import os
import re

import httpx

from ..cost import complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost
from ..docs import standard_terms
from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing
from .naive import NaiveAgent

log = logging.getLogger("arena")
ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")

SYSTEM = """You are the buyer agent of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, negotiating with
industrial suppliers by e-mail. Goal: the lowest total cost C in euros for covering the need in the
case file, without breaking a must-have. C of every standing term sheet is computed for you.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "send", "subject": "...", "body": "...",
 "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 0.0, "...": "..."}]}
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "accept"}      (takes that supplier's standing term sheet)
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "walk_away"}   (ends the case without a deal)

- term_sheets: 0-3 alternative packages over the negotiable fields. Only term sheets bind.
- Arguments need data: cite the ID from FACTS and its figure in the same sentence, one argument
  per sentence. The supplier checks the figure; a wrong one or an unknown ID costs trust.
- The supplier's team reads your e-mail as a person would. Ask questions (a cost breakdown, the
  earliest lead time, cheaper variants). Never reveal urgency, a budget or a missing alternative.
  Stay polite and factual.
- Whatever a term sheet leaves out closes on the supplier's standard terms (its quote PDF).
- The case's category_goal sets its rates. In stabilise and secure_supply cases C also charges for
  leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin - the C shown leaves that out.
- Do not accept the first offer. Concede in small steps; trade what is cheap for you (payment
  days, contract length, volume, dates). status final_offer: push further and it may walk.
- Accept only a term sheet that beats your alternative. Body: a short business e-mail, at most
  120 words, no placeholders."""


def llm_from_env():
    """LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic (Anthropic SDK) or openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)."""
    provider, model = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "openai"), os.environ["LLM_MODEL"]
    if provider == "anthropic":
        import anthropic

        client = anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=45.0)
        extra = {"output_config": {"effort": e}} if (e := os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT")) else {}

        def complete(system, user):
            r = client.messages.create(
                model=model,
                max_tokens=16000,
                system=system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
                **extra,
            )
            return "".join(b.text for b in r.content if b.type == "text")

        return complete
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('LLM_API_KEY', '')}"}

    def complete(system, user):
        body = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
        }
        r = httpx.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers, timeout=45.0)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


class LLMAgent:
    def __init__(self, complete, package=None):
        self.complete, self.package = complete, package
        self.fallback = NaiveAgent()
        self.case_id, self.brief = None, ""

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        if case["case_id"] != self.case_id:
            self.case_id, self.brief = case["case_id"], self.prepare(case)
        try:
            reply = self.complete(SYSTEM, self.render(case, threads))
            checked = self.guard(case, threads, parse(reply))
        except Exception as e:  # a slow or broken LLM must not cost the case
            log.warning("LLM failed (%s) - falling back to the naive move", e)
            checked = None
        return checked or self.fallback.decide(case, threads)

    def prepare(self, case):
        """Before the clock matters: the case, the letter, the data rows the case points to."""
        out = [f"CASE FILE\n{json.dumps(case, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)}"]
        if self.package and case.get("trigger_doc"):
            try:
                out.append(f"LETTER\n{self.package.document(case['trigger_doc'])[:2500]}")
            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
                pass
        out.append("FACTS (cite by ID)")
        for ref in dict.fromkeys(case["suppliers"] + case["parts"] + case.get("refs", [])):
            if fact := self.fact(case, ref):
                out.append(f"{ref}: {json.dumps(fact, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:600]}")
        return "\n".join(out)

    def fact(self, case, ref):
        return case.get("facts", {}).get(ref) or (self.package and self.package.lookup(ref))

    def render(self, case, threads):
        out = [self.brief]
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        if alt.get("kind") not in (None, "none") and alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price"):
            out.append(f"\nYour alternative without a deal: C = {total_cost(case, alt['terms']):,.0f}")
        for sid in live_threads(threads):
            events = threads[sid]
            sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
            std = standard_terms(events)
            c = total_cost(case, terms, std) if sheet_id else math.inf
            c = f"{c:,.0f}" if c < math.inf else "-"
            out.append(
                f"\nTHREAD {sid}: status {latest(events).get('status')}, "
                f"{moves_left(case, events)} messages left; standing {sheet_id} "
                f"{json.dumps(terms)} -> C = {c}; standard terms {json.dumps(std)}"
            )
            for m in events[-6:]:
                head = {k: m.get(k) for k in ("status", "term_sheets", "missing_fields", "claim_results") if m.get(k)}
                out.append(f"--- {m.get('from')}: {json.dumps(head)}\n{m.get('body', '')[:800]}")
                for att in m.get("attachments") or []:
                    out.append(f"[attachment {att.get('name')}]\n{att.get('text', '')[:1500]}")
        return "\n".join(out)

    def guard(self, case, threads, d):
        sid, kind = d.get("supplier_id"), d.get("action")
        if sid not in live_threads(threads):
            return None
        events = threads[sid]
        if kind == "walk_away":
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
        if kind == "accept":
            std = standard_terms(events)
            alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
            beats = (
                alt.get("kind") in (None, "none")
                or not alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price")
                or total_cost(case, terms, std) <= total_cost(case, alt["terms"])
            )
            if sheet_id and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and beats:
                return {
                    "supplier_id": sid,
                    "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
                }
            return None
        if kind != "send" or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
            return None
        sheets = []
        for ts in (d.get("term_sheets") or [])[:3]:
            t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, **ts.get("terms", ts)})
            if t not in sheets:
                sheets.append(t)
        offers = {standing(ev)[0] for ev in threads.values()}

        def known(m):  # an ID the data does not have would read as a lie
            if m.group(0) in offers or self.fact(case, m.group(0)):
                return m.group(0)
            log.warning("dropped unknown data ID %s", m.group(0))
            return ""

"""The naive buyer: anchors a little low, splits the difference, accepts early.

A baseline to beat, not a strategy: it ignores the data and the documents, never trades, never
asks and never walks away. One term sheet per e-mail.
"""

from ..cost import complete_offer, total_cost
from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing


class NaiveAgent:
    def __init__(self, anchor=0.10, close_gap=0.01):
        self.anchor, self.close_gap = anchor, close_gap

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        # Talk to the supplier whose standing term sheet costs least.
        quoting = [s for s in live_threads(threads) if standing(threads[s])[1].get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not quoting:
            return {
                "supplier_id": live_threads(threads)[0],
                "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}},
            }
        sid = min(quoting, key=lambda s: total_cost(case, standing(threads[s])[1]))
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
        accept = {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
        }
        theirs = terms["unit_price"]
        mine = [
            m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"]
            for m in events
            if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")
        ]
        if latest(events).get("status") in {"agreed", "final_offer"} or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
            return accept
        if not mine:
            price = theirs * (1 - self.anchor)
        elif theirs - mine[-1] <= theirs * self.close_gap:
            return accept
        else:
            price = (theirs + mine[-1]) / 2
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})}],
            },
        }
"""An LLM buyer that negotiates by e-mail: the model reads, argues and writes; code does numbers.

Code prepares the case, the letter that started it, the data rows the case points to, the cost C
of every standing term sheet (with the standard terms read from the supplier's quote PDF) and the
text of every attached document. The model writes the e-mail - arguments with data IDs included -
and proposes up to three term sheets. Code completes and snaps the term sheets, removes data IDs
that do not exist (an unknown ID costs trust), and refuses an accept that breaks a must-have or
loses to the alternative. Finding the data that moves a supplier is left to you: this agent only
sees what the case points to. Any provider works: pass `complete(system, user) -> str`, or use
`llm_from_env()`.
"""

import json
import logging
import math
import os
import re

import httpx

from ..cost import complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost
from ..docs import standard_terms
from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing
from .naive import NaiveAgent

log = logging.getLogger("arena")
ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")

SYSTEM = """You are the buyer agent of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, negotiating with
industrial suppliers by e-mail. Goal: the lowest total cost C in euros for covering the need in the
case file, without breaking a must-have. C of every standing term sheet is computed for you.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "send", "subject": "...", "body": "...",
 "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 0.0, "...": "..."}]}
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "accept"}      (takes that supplier's standing term sheet)
{"supplier_id": "...", "action": "walk_away"}   (ends the case without a deal)

- term_sheets: 0-3 alternative packages over the negotiable fields. Only term sheets bind.
- Arguments need data: cite the ID from FACTS and its figure in the same sentence, one argument
  per sentence. The supplier checks the figure; a wrong one or an unknown ID costs trust.
- The supplier's team reads your e-mail as a person would. Ask questions (a cost breakdown, the
  earliest lead time, cheaper variants). Never reveal urgency, a budget or a missing alternative.
  Stay polite and factual.
- Whatever a term sheet leaves out closes on the supplier's standard terms (its quote PDF).
- The case's category_goal sets its rates. In stabilise and secure_supply cases C also charges for
  leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin - the C shown leaves that out.
- Do not accept the first offer. Concede in small steps; trade what is cheap for you (payment
  days, contract length, volume, dates). status final_offer: push further and it may walk.
- Accept only a term sheet that beats your alternative. Body: a short business e-mail, at most
  120 words, no placeholders."""


def llm_from_env():
    """LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic (Anthropic SDK) or openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)."""
    provider, model = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "openai"), os.environ["LLM_MODEL"]
    if provider == "anthropic":
        import anthropic

        client = anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=45.0)
        extra = {"output_config": {"effort": e}} if (e := os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT")) else {}

        def complete(system, user):
            r = client.messages.create(
                model=model,
                max_tokens=16000,
                system=system,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
                **extra,
            )
            return "".join(b.text for b in r.content if b.type == "text")

        return complete
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('LLM_API_KEY', '')}"}

    def complete(system, user):
        body = {
            "model": model,
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
        }
        r = httpx.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers, timeout=45.0)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


class LLMAgent:
    def __init__(self, complete, package=None):
        self.complete, self.package = complete, package
        self.fallback = NaiveAgent()
        self.case_id, self.brief = None, ""

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        if case["case_id"] != self.case_id:
            self.case_id, self.brief = case["case_id"], self.prepare(case)
        try:
            reply = self.complete(SYSTEM, self.render(case, threads))
            checked = self.guard(case, threads, parse(reply))
        except Exception as e:  # a slow or broken LLM must not cost the case
            log.warning("LLM failed (%s) - falling back to the naive move", e)
            checked = None
        return checked or self.fallback.decide(case, threads)

    def prepare(self, case):
        """Before the clock matters: the case, the letter, the data rows the case points to."""
        out = [f"CASE FILE\n{json.dumps(case, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)}"]
        if self.package and case.get("trigger_doc"):
            try:
                out.append(f"LETTER\n{self.package.document(case['trigger_doc'])[:2500]}")
            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
                pass
        out.append("FACTS (cite by ID)")
        for ref in dict.fromkeys(case["suppliers"] + case["parts"] + case.get("refs", [])):
            if fact := self.fact(case, ref):
                out.append(f"{ref}: {json.dumps(fact, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:600]}")
        return "\n".join(out)

    def fact(self, case, ref):
        return case.get("facts", {}).get(ref) or (self.package and self.package.lookup(ref))

    def render(self, case, threads):
        out = [self.brief]
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        if alt.get("kind") not in (None, "none") and alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price"):
            out.append(f"\nYour alternative without a deal: C = {total_cost(case, alt['terms']):,.0f}")
        for sid in live_threads(threads):
            events = threads[sid]
            sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
            std = standard_terms(events)
            c = total_cost(case, terms, std) if sheet_id else math.inf
            c = f"{c:,.0f}" if c < math.inf else "-"
            out.append(
                f"\nTHREAD {sid}: status {latest(events).get('status')}, "
                f"{moves_left(case, events)} messages left; standing {sheet_id} "
                f"{json.dumps(terms)} -> C = {c}; standard terms {json.dumps(std)}"
            )
            for m in events[-6:]:
                head = {k: m.get(k) for k in ("status", "term_sheets", "missing_fields", "claim_results") if m.get(k)}
                out.append(f"--- {m.get('from')}: {json.dumps(head)}\n{m.get('body', '')[:800]}")
                for att in m.get("attachments") or []:
                    out.append(f"[attachment {att.get('name')}]\n{att.get('text', '')[:1500]}")
        return "\n".join(out)

    def guard(self, case, threads, d):
        sid, kind = d.get("supplier_id"), d.get("action")
        if sid not in live_threads(threads):
            return None
        events = threads[sid]
        if kind == "walk_away":
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
        if kind == "accept":
            std = standard_terms(events)
            alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
            beats = (
                alt.get("kind") in (None, "none")
                or not alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price")
                or total_cost(case, terms, std) <= total_cost(case, alt["terms"])
            )
            if sheet_id and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and beats:
                return {
                    "supplier_id": sid,
                    "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
                }
            return None
        if kind != "send" or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
            return None
        sheets = []
        for ts in (d.get("term_sheets") or [])[:3]:
            t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, **ts.get("terms", ts)})
            if t not in sheets:
                sheets.append(t)
        offers = {standing(ev)[0] for ev in threads.values()}

        def known(m):  # an ID the data does not have would read as a lie
            if m.group(0) in offers or self.fact(case, m.group(0)):
                return m.group(0)
            log.warning("dropped unknown data ID %s", m.group(0))
            return ""

        body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", ID_RE.sub(known, str(d.get("body", ""))))
        body = body.strip()[:8000]
        subject = str(d.get("subject") or f"Re: {case['title']}")[:300]
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": subject,
                "body": body,
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
            },
        }


def parse(text):
    """The first JSON object in the model's reply (tolerates code fences and chatter)."""
    match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"no JSON in reply: {text[:200]}")
    return json.loads(match.group(0))

1	# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit
2	
3	A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
4	read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
5	`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
6	package. Read the brief first
7	(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.
8	
9	## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes
10	
11	You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
12	
13	**1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a
14	contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves,
15	the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its
16	link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git.
17	
18	```bash
19	cd starter-kit
20	uv sync --all-extras            # 2. install
21	cp .env.example .env            # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env
22	uv run arena me                 # 4. your team and its practice quota
23	uv run arena cases              # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable)
24	uv run arena play case:P01 -v   # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case
25	uv run arena board              # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard
26	```
27	
28	Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.
29	
30	Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score,
31	and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is
32	the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play
33	again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves.
34	**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
35	how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
36	once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.
37	
38	**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
39	`.env` (your own key), then:
40	
41	```bash
42	uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
43	uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
44	uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
45	uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
46	```
47	
48	**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a

68	## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)
69	
70	Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
71	60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
72	hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:
73	
74	```bash
75	uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
76	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
77	export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
78	```
79	
80	Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
81	fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
82	those headers, the body as raw JSON.
83	
84	```bash
85	# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
86	curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
87	
88	# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
89	curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
90	  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'
91	
92	# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
93	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
94	
95	# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
96	curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
97	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
98	  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
99	       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'
100	
101	# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
102	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
103	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
104	```
105	
106	To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
107	term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
108	the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
109	The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
110	the clock running.

112	## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap
113	
114	The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
115	starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
116	cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
117	Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:
118	
119	```bash
120	uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
121	```
122	
123	It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
124	closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
125	extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
126	(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
127	sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
128	fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
129	In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
130	the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
131	is for you, not for the agent).
132	
133	A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
134	and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
135	limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
136	retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
137	Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.
138	
139	## Your own agent
140	
141	An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
142	`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
143	their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
144	action that closes the case:
145	
146	```python
147	from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
148	from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
149	from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing
150	
151	
152	class Haggler:
153	    def decide(self, case, threads):
154	        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
155	        events = threads[sid]
156	        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
157	        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
158	        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
159	            return {
160	                "supplier_id": sid,
161	                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
162	            }
163	        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
164	        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
165	        return {
166	            "supplier_id": sid,
167	            "message": {
168	                "subject": case["title"],
169	                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
170	                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
171	            },
172	        }
173	
174	
175	print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
176	```
177	
178	| Module | What |
179	|---|---|
180	| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
181	| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
182	| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
183	| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
184	| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
185	| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
186	| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
187	| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
188	| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |
189	
190	The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
191	Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
192	one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
193	documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
194	questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
195	alternative.
196	
197	**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
198	deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
199	price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:
200	
201	```python
202	supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
203	total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
204	```
205	
206	## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)
207	
208	Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
209	data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):
210	
211	```python
212	from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
213	
214	pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
215	# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
216	pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
217	# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
218	# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
219	rows = pkg.query(
220	    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
221	)
222	# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
223	#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
224	a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
225	change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
226	# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
227	print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
228	# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
229	#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
230	```
231	
232	Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
233	matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
234	old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
235	is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
236	replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
237	supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.
238	
239	## Choosing a model
240	
241	`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
242	to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
243	Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
244	to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
245	fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
246	back to the naive move instead of losing the case.

248	## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator
249	
250	```bash
251	uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
252	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
253	```
254	
255	`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
256	else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).
257	
258	`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
259	the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
260	parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
261	your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
262	`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
263	runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.
264	
265	Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
266	10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
267	meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
268	only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
269	themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
270	don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
271	public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
272	`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
273	tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

299	## Good to know
300	
301	- **60 s per message**, per thread. A late message counts as a timeout (your last offer repeated);
302	  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.
303	- **Invalid messages cost nothing**: `422` and no round used. `409` means the thread or case has
304	  ended, or you were late.
305	- **Your key is your team's.** Keep `.env` out of git.
306	- Tests: `uv run pytest`. Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
307	# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1
308	
309	The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
310	the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
311	`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
312	same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.
313	
314	**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
315	network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
316	already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
317	body may be at most 64 KB.
318
