325	## Flow
326	
327	```
328	GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
329	GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
330	GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
331	POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
332	POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
333	GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
334	POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
335	GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
336	```
337	
338	## Endpoints
339	
340	### Your key
341	
342	One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
343	contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
344	approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
345	(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).
346	
347	Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
348	revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
349	There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
350	organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).
351	
352	### `GET /v1/me`
353	
354	Where your team stands:
355	
356	```json
357	{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
358	 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
359	 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
360	```
361	`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
362	(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.
363	
364	### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`
365	
366	A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.
367	
368	| Set | Cases | Replay |
369	|---|---|---|
370	| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
371	| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
372	| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |
373	
374	The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
375	results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
376	names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).
377	
378	### `POST /v1/sessions`
379	
380	`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
381	from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.
382	
383	| Response field | |
384	|---|---|
385	| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
386	| `case` | the case file |
387	| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
388	| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |
389	
390	Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
391	**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
392	answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
393	starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
394	retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
395	pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.
396	
397	### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`
398	
399	Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
400	With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
401	`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
402	`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.
403	
404	A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
405	seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
406	
407	`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
408	negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
409	than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
410	you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
411	as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.
412	
413	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`
414	
415	The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
416	ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
417	"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
418	after a crash.
419	
420	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`
421	
422	The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
423	data. See [Documents](#documents).
424	
425	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`
426	
427	The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
428	(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
429	(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
430	`result` and `replay_url`.
431	
432	### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`
433	
434	The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
435	same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
436	ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.
437	
438	### Lists and boards
439	
440	- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
441	- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
442	  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
443	  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
444	  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
445	  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.
446	
447	- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
448	  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
449	- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
450	  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
451	  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
452	  ```json
453	  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
454	   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
455	              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
456	              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
457	   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
458	  ```
459	  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
460	  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
461	  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
462	  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
463	  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
464	  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
465	  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
466	  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
467	  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
468	  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
469	  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
470	  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
471	  - they are for people.
472	- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
473	  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
474	  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
475	  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
476	  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
477	  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
478	  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
479	- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
480	  practice records and highlights.
481	- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
482	  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
483	  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
484	  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.
485	
486	### The structured path
487	
488	For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
489	{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
490	"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
491	{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
492	(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.
493	
494	## Messages
495	
496	| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
497	|---|---|---|
498	| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
499	| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
500	| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
501	| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
502	| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
503	| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
504	| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
505	| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
506	| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
507	| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
508	| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
509	| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |
510	
511	A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.
512	
513	A real exchange from practice case `case:P01` (Brandlhuber announces +9.5 % on volute casings,
514	"due to energy and wages"); the starter kit's README shows how the index figure was found:
515	
516	```json
517	{"message": {
518	  "subject": "HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
519	  "body": "Dear Sir or Madam,\nthank you for your letter. We cannot follow +9.5 % from November.\nElectricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).\nCould you send us a cost breakdown?\nBest regards\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing",
520	  "term_sheets": [
521	    {"terms": {"unit_price": 129.90, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 60}},
522	    {"terms": {"unit_price": 128.50, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 14}}]}}
523	```
524	→
525	```json
526	{"thread_id": "thread:P01:70110", "message_id": "msg:70110-1-2", "from": "sales@70110",
527	 "subject": "Re: HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
528	 "body": "Guten Tag,\nYour requested terms change our costs; our Angebot for them follows.\nPreis €139.80 per unit, Zahlungsziel 14 Tage netto, valid from 2027-04-01.\nWe checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.\nWe did not know that - a fair point.\nLCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 30 % of our cost. That remains.\nPPI-C241 rose 6.5 % in twelve months and is 24 % of our cost. That remains.\nFaster payment helps our cash flow; that is reflected in the price.\nOur costs move with LCI-C, PPI-C241, PPI-D351; the figures stay with us.\nViele Grüße aus der Gießerei\nGießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG",
529	 "status": "open",
530	 "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:70110-1",
531	                  "terms": {"unit_price": 139.80, "payment_days": 14, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"}}],
532	 "missing_fields": [], "claim_results": [{"index": 0, "result": "verified"}],
533	 "signals": {"reply_delay_days": 2, "validity_days": 30}, "attachments": []}
534	```
535	The supplier answered the 14-day sheet at its own price for an April start, accepted the index
536	figure - and answered with the cost drivers that rose. (Offline wording from a local run; on the
537	hosted arena the supplier writes its own e-mail and may well decide differently.)
538	
539	## What counts
540	
541	**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
542	prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.
543	
544	**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
545	in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
546	check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
547	Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
548	three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
549	are context, not checks.
550	
551	| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
552	|---|---|---|
553	| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
554	| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
555	| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
556	| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
557	| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
558	| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |
559	
560	Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
561	data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
562	true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
563	`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
564	once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
565	counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
566	supplier you cite it to.
567	
568	**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
569	and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
570	from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
571	or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
572	letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.
573	
574	**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
575	alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
576	as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
577	company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.
578	
579	## Documents
580	
581	Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.
582	
583	| Document | When | What matters |
584	|---|---|---|
585	| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
586	| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
587	| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
588	| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
589	| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |
590	
591	## Terms
592	
593	Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
594	`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
595	a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).
596	
597	| Field | Type | Meaning |
598	|---|---|---|
599	| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
600	| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
601	| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
602	| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
603	| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
604	| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
605	| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
606	| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
607	| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
608	| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
609	| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |
610	
611	## Case file
612	
613	Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
614	any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.
615	
616	| Field | |
617	|---|---|
618	| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
619	| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
620	| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
621	| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
622	| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
623	| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
624	| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
625	| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
626	| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |
627	
628	`buyer`:
629	
630	| Field | |
631	|---|---|
632	| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
633	| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
634	| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
635	| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
636	| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
637	| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
638	| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
639	| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
640	| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
641	| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
642	| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
643	| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
644	| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
645	| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |
646	
647	## Data IDs
648	
649	IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
650	column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
651	checks:
652	
653	| ID | Fields |
654	|---|---|
655	| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
656	| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
657	| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
658	| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
659	| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
660	| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
661	| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
662	| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
663	| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
664	| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |
665	
666	Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.
667	
668	## Result, trace and back office
669	
670	Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
671	end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
672	`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.
673	
674	| Field | |
675	|---|---|
676	| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
677	| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
678	| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
679	| `score` | 0-1 |
680	| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
681	| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |
682	
683	## Cost and score
684	
685	With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
686	`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:
687	
688	```
689	years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
690	committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
691	covered   = min(V, N) · years
692	pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
693	new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
694	spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
695	uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
696	C = spend
697	  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
698	  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
699	  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
700	  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
701	  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
702	  + tooling_eur
703	  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
704	  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
705	  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
706	                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
707	soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
708	```
709	
710	The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
711	expected move of the clause's series.
712	
713	**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
714	full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
715	standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
716	the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
717	(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
718	really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
719	brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
720	So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
721	You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
722	you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
723	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.
724	
725	```
726	score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
727	```
728	
729	`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
730	of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
731	lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
732	− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.
733	
734	## Live Final in waves
735	
736	The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
737	starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
738	Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
739	`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
740	wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
741	the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:
742	
743	| Field | |
744	|---|---|
745	| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
746	| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
747	| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |
748	
749	Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
750	/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
751	`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
752	deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
753	0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
754	list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
755	--set final` in the starter kit does this.
756	
757	## Time, errors and limits
758	
759	- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
760	  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
761	  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
762	  thread.
763	- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
764	  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
765	- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
766	  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.
767	
768	| Status | When |
769	|---|---|
770	| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
771	| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
772	| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
773	| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
774	| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
775	| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
776	| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |
777	
778	Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.
779

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit

A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
package. Read the brief first
(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.

## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

**1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves,
the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its
link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git.

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --all-extras            # 2. install
cp .env.example .env            # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env
uv run arena me                 # 4. your team and its practice quota
uv run arena cases              # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable)
uv run arena play case:P01 -v   # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case
uv run arena board              # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard
```

Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.

Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score,
and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is
the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play
again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves.
**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.

**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
`.env` (your own key), then:

```bash
uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
```

**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a
memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them.

No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs.
The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After
`uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above):

# terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`)

ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key

## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)

Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
```

Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
those headers, the body as raw JSON.

```bash
# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'

# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'

# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
the clock running.

## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap

The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
is for you, not for the agent).

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

## Choosing a model

`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
back to the naive move instead of losing the case.

## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
```

`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).

`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.

Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

## MCP server over the data

A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,
`get_case`.

```bash
uv run arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package   # speaks MCP on stdin/stdout
```

Add it to a client, e.g. Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add arena-data -- uv run --directory /path/to/starter-kit arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package
```

or any client with an `mcpServers` config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"arena-data": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/starter-kit",
  "arena", "mcp", "--data", "/path/to/data/package"]}}}
```

## Good to know

- **60 s per message**, per thread. A late message counts as a timeout (your last offer repeated);
  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.
- **Invalid messages cost nothing**: `422` and no round used. `409` means the thread or case has
  ended, or you were late.
- **Your key is your team's.** Keep `.env` out of git.
- Tests: `uv run pytest`. Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

### Lists and boards

- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.

- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |

| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Data IDs

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

## Result, trace and back office

Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |

Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.

content.text:
I've read the brief, API docs, both example agents and our P01 replay. I can't run an LLM agent yet: there is no LLM key in `.env` or your shell (only a local `ollama` binary).

**What the scoring and the P01 replay show**

- **Score is total cost, not price.** Payment days, effective date, contract length, volume, freight, defect commitments and index clauses all count in euros, and the kit's `total_cost` computes it offline for any term sheet.
- **Squeezing some suppliers is penalised.** In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases (P01, P02, P03, P10) the cost also charges for leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin.
- **Our 0.58 on P01 was pure haggling.** The naive agent cited no data, never touched `effective_date`, and accepted after four small concessions. The supplier's stated reasons were labour and steel indices, which we never challenged.
- **The Discord targets are multi-lever cases.** P02 (copper) and P08 (alloy surcharge) both have `index_clause` as a negotiable field, which is probably why the board's best scores there are 0.29 and 0.23 against house scores around 0.75.
- **The final rewards generalising.** Up to a third of hidden cases combine supplier and case types practice never shows, so per-case tuning on P01–P19 won't carry over.

**What I'd build**

1. A code layer that scores every term sheet with `total_cost` and searches the allowed options for the cheapest package per case, so the model never does arithmetic.
2. A per-supplier dossier built before the session opens: notes, letters, news, scorecards, index moves with checkable IDs, should-cost.
3. An LLM that only reads the supplier and writes the e-mail, with guards against bad accepts and unknown IDs, as the kit's `llm.py` already does.

Developing against the sandbox cases D01/D02 is free; practice quota is at 199 of 200.

**What I need from you**

- Which LLM provider and model to use, with the key added to `starter-kit/.env` (`LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `LLM_API_KEY`). Each message must go out within 60 seconds of the supplier's reply, so a fast model matters more than a big one.

Until then I can build steps 1 and 2, which need no LLM — say go and I'll start there.

AGENTS.md# EHL monorepo

Two independent apps plus PostgreSQL, orchestrated with Docker Compose. Frontend and backend share no code,
dependencies or tooling; they talk over HTTP only.

```
frontend/   Next.js 16 · React 19 · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · pnpm   (DESIGN.md = UI style reference)
backend/    Python 3.13 · uv · FastAPI · SQLAlchemy 2 (async) · Alembic
docker-compose.yml   db (postgres:17) · backend · frontend
```

## Run everything

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # optional: override ports and DB credentials
docker compose up --build
```

- Frontend: http://localhost:3000
- Backend API: http://localhost:8000/api, OpenAPI docs at http://localhost:8000/docs
- PostgreSQL: localhost:5432 (`app`/`app`)

The backend container runs `alembic upgrade head` on start. The frontend proxies `/api/*` to the backend, so
the browser only ever talks to the frontend. Networks are split: the frontend can reach the backend but not
the database.

## Develop locally (database in Docker, apps on the host)

```sh
git submodule update --init   # negotiation-arena-kit/
make install                  # uv sync + pnpm install
make db                       # PostgreSQL on localhost:5432
make backend                  # terminal 1: migrations + fastapi dev  -> http://localhost:8000/docs
make frontend                 # terminal 2: next dev                  -> http://localhost:3000
make test && make lint
```

Both dev servers reload on save. `make up` / `make down` run the whole stack in Docker instead.

## Backend: three layers

```
src/app/
  api/            presentation: routes, request/response handling, dependency wiring (deps.py)
  services/       business logic and rules; raises ServiceError subclasses, mapped to HTTP in main.py
  repositories/   data access: SQLAlchemy queries, nothing else
  models/         ORM models (tables)
  schemas/        Pydantic DTOs for the API
  core/           settings and database engine/session
```

Each request gets a session (`core/database.py`) → repository → service → route. Services never touch HTTP or
SQL directly, so they are unit-tested with an in-memory fake repository (`tests/test_item_service.py`).
`items` is an example resource showing the pattern end to end.

```sh
cd backend
uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format .
